The present petition has been filed seeking quashing of FIR No.1424/2014 under Sections 498A/406/323/506 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (IPC) and Section 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act,
1961 registered at Police Station Hari Nagar on the ground of settlement.
2. The petitioner is the husband of the respondent no.2.
The marriage of the petitioner and the respondent no.2 was solemnized on 1st March, 2006 as per Hindu rites and ceremonies.
No child was born out of the wedlock.
3. Dispute arose between the petitioner and the respondent no.2, which resulted in filing of the present FIR by the respondent no.2 against the petitioner.

4. Now the parties have settled all their disputes before the Delhi Mediation Centre, Tis Hazari Courts, Delhi, in terms of Settlement Deed dated 11th August, 2023, which has been filed as Annexure P-2 to the This is a digitally signed order.

sentences.text: As per the settlement, the parties have decided to obtain divorce by mutual consent.
The first motion has already been allowed vide order dated 16th September, 2023.
6. Issue notice.

7. Notice is accepted by the learned APP appearing on behalf of the State and the counsel appearing on behalf of the respondent no.2.
8.
The respondent no.2 is present in Court and has been identified by her counsel as well as by the Investigating Officer (IO).
She informs the Court that she has settled the matter of her own free will and without any coercion.
She further states that she has no objection to quashing of the FIR.
9. The petitioner is also present in Court and has been identified by his counsel.

He affirms the statement of the respondent no.2 and undertakes to abide by the terms of settlement arrived at between the parties.
10.

Considering the above settlement between the parties and the chances of conviction of the petitioner being remote and bleak, there is no use continuing with proceedings of the present FIR as it would be a misuse of the process of the Court and an unnecessary burden on the State exchequer.
Hence, it would be in the interest of justice to quash the aforementioned FIR and the proceedings pursuant thereto.
11. Consequently, the FIR No.1424/2014 registered at Police Station Hari Nagar and the proceedings pursuant thereto are quashed.
12. The petition stands disposed of.
AMIT BANSAL, J OCTOBER 17, 2023 sr
